title: The Mexican Left’s War on NGOs
author: Juan David Rojas
content:
![The Mexican Left’s War on
NGOs](https://www.compactmag.com/content/images/2026/03/AP26078720336719.jpg)

Over the weekend, Mexico's Internal Revenue Service (SAT) rescinded tax
permits for more than [_100 NGOs_](https://www.eluniversal.com.mx/nacion/sat-
cancela-permiso-para-donativos-a-mas-de-100-ong-mexicanos-primero-y-mexico-
evalua-entre-las-afectadas/?ref=compactmag.com), terminating their ability to
receive donations and qualify for tax exemptions. Many have a path to
restoring their NGO status, but around a dozen were liquidated outright for
failing to comply with fiscal rules. These moves form part of a broad
crackdown on waste and foreign interference in Mexico by the ruling left-wing
Morena party under President Claudia Sheinbaum and her predecessor Andres
Manuel Lopez Obrador (AMLO).

The Mexican opposition and its allies in the international press have decried
these actions as proof of the country's alleged "democratic backsliding." In
reality, opposition-aligned NGOs like Mexicanos Contra La Corrupcion y la
Impunidad (MCCI) form part of an artificial civil society complex that was
funded, in part, by the now defunct USAID. Upon assuming office in 2018, one
of AMLO's first initiatives was to restore state control over functions that
previous governments had devolved to NGOs and private companies. His
administration [_slashed_](https://www.eleconomista.com.mx/opinion/ONGs-AMLO-
nunca-las-quiso-y-ahora-liquidara-a-la-
mayoria-20211020-0151.html?ref=compactmag.com) over $300 million of state
support for NGOs and reclassified all contractors as state employees,
effectively ending their role in government.

Since 2013, Mexico's [_Anti-Money Laundering
Statute_](https://www.adlercolvin.com/blog/2015/04/21/mexicos-anti-money-
laundering-law-affects-u-s-donors/?ref=compactmag.com) has required NGOs that
receive more than $7,000 in donations to reveal the identities of individual
donors; those that receive over $15,000 must report individual transactions to
authorities. These restrictions were geared towards combating organized crime
amid the country's ongoing drug war. Before Morena came to power, the
country's tax authority exercised loose oversight of foreign funding for NGOs,
much as it allowed corporations and the wealthy to skirt their [_tax
obligations_](https://www.compactmag.com/article/will-mexicos-elon-musk-
succeed/).

AMLO's and Sheinbaum's crackdowns on tax evasion and strict enforcement of NGO
regulations have prompted figures like MCCI founder Claudio X. Gonzalez to
accuse Morena of running a
"[_narcodictatorship_](https://www.lavozdemichoacan.com.mx/mexico/ruta2024/claudio-
x-gonzalez-alarmado-por-posible-dictadura-y-narcoestado-si-gana-
sheinbaum/?ref=compactmag.com)." This claim has been picked up north of the
border by Republicans and many liberals, despite the fact that the Washington-
aligned PRI and PAN governments that preceded Morena are known to have had
deep [_cartel ties_](https://www.nytimes.com/es/topic/genaro-garcia-
luna?ref=compactmag.com). But the average Mexican will tell you that the
cartels are only one powerful interest group exerting a corrupting influence
on the nation's politics, and foreign-backed NGOs are another.

Much of the funding for entities like MCCI**** ultimately traced back to
donations from [_USAID_](https://contralinea.com.mx/interno/semana/imco-y-
mexico-evalua-opositores-financiados-por-eu-y-burguesia-
mexicana/?ref=compactmag.com) and the libertarian [_Atlas
Network_](https://jornadaveracruz.com.mx/atlas-network-la-fabrica-global-del-
sabotaje-libertario/?ref=compactmag.com). All told, foreign financing of NGOs
rose [_56 percent_](https://www.milenio.com/politica/financiamiento-
extranjero-a-ongs-aumento-en-sexenio-de-amlo?ref=compactmag.com) during AMLO's
presidency to over half a billion dollars, more than offsetting his cuts to
state funding. Sheinbaum is now following Lopez Obrador's example by ensuring
that NGOs comply with pertinent regulations.

Sheinbaum has been less openly antagonistic to international progressivism
than her predecessor, whose heresies on everything from climate change to
[_gender
norms_](https://www.larazon.es/internacional/20200626/w5sqtew2yre7jjtgbpnks3azl4.html?ref=compactmag.com)
attracted the ire of identitarian leftists. In contrast, progressives abroad
are entranced by Mexico's first female and climate scientist president, who
boasts a roughly [_70 percent_](https://www.as-coa.org/articles/approval-
tracker-mexicos-president-claudia-sheinbaum?ref=compactmag.com) approval
rating at home. But they might have been surprised had they noticed that the
Mexican leader [_celebrated_](https://www.newsweek.com/trump-musk-unexpected-
ally-push-shut-down-usaid-2026231?ref=compactmag.com) the virtual dismantling
of USAID by Elon Musk's DOGE.

Sheinbaum's government is also quietly expanding
[_fracking_](https://elpais.com/mexico/2026-02-18/sheinbaum-reconoce-que-el-
uso-de-fracking-en-mexico-esta-a-discusion.html?ref=compactmag.com) in tandem
with renewables while overseeing a [_rail
renaissance_](https://polemon.mx/claudia-sheinbaum-se-compromete-a-
construir-3-nuevas-rutas-de-trenes-de-pasajeros/?ref=compactmag.com) over the
opposition of green NGOs and activist groups. She and her security minister,
Omar Garcia Harfuch, have also undertaken arguably the most aggressive
offensive against organized crime in the country's history. On February 22,
Mexican special forces executed CJNG cartel kingpin Nemesio Oseguera
Cervantes, alias "El Mencho," and this month, authorities killed [_eleven
members_](https://www.dw.com/es/al-menos-11-muertos-en-operativo-militar-
contra-el-cartel-de-sinaloa/a-76442606?ref=compactmag.com) of the Sinaloa
cartel in Culiacan. These accomplishments would not have been possible were it
not for Morena's decoupling from NGO-funded professional-class elites and
crackdowns on foreign meddling.

> "The Democratic Party is deeply enmeshed with the NGO-industrial complex"

In contrast, the progressive wing of the Democratic Party is deeply enmeshed
with the NGO-industrial complex--hence the shock and horror expressed over the
dismantling of USAID. The result is the outsourcing of governance to
unaccountable, parasitic NGOs that function as a jobs program for college-
educated professionals while offering little to the working-class voters the
party claims to represent. The worst thing Zohran Mamdani could do as New York
mayor is follow the example of other progressive enclaves and spin grocery
stores [_administered by NGOs_](https://economicsecurityproject.org/news/the-
washington-post-new-york-might-experiment-with-city-run-grocery-stores-how-do-
they-
work/?ref=compactmag.com#:~:text=Yes%2C%20but%20only%20a%20handful,to%20become%20profitable%2C%20she%20said.)
as "state-run." Those who seek to reorient the party in a populist direction
should learn from AMLO and Sheinbaum by cutting off "the groups" and
scrutinizing those that receive foreign funding.
